kaps_punt: Die name van provinsies en hul hoofstede op 'n kaart - 1 uur

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika is in nege provinsies verdeel, en elkeen het sy eie regering.
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' (https://www.gov.za/about-sa/south-africas-provinces): nine provinces; 'Each province has its own Legislature, Premier and Executive Council.'

items.bewering: Elke provinsie se regering sit in 'n stad wat ons sy hoofstad noem.
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' - a capital is listed for each of the nine provinces.

items.bewering: Gauteng: Johannesburg; Limpopo: Polokwane; Mpumalanga: Mbombela; Noordwes: Mahikeng; Vrystaat: Bloemfontein; KwaZulu-Natal: Pietermaritzburg; Oos-Kaap: Bhisho; Noord-Kaap: Kimberley; Wes-Kaap: Kaapstad
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' - all nine capitals match exactly, including the current spellings Mbombela, Mahikeng and Bhisho. Also GCIS Pocket Guide 'Provinces'.

items.bewering: Twaalf sulke wêrelderfenisterreine lê oor Suid-Afrika versprei.
items.bron: SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/69965) and The Presidency (gov.za media statement, July 2024): the two 2024 inscriptions brought South Africa to 12. The 47th session (Paris, July 2025) added no new South African property, only the Maputo National Park extension of iSimangaliso; no South African inscription found among the 25 of the 48th session (Busan, July 2026) per UNESCO news 2915 and Bizcommunity.

items.bewering: Vier is op die lys vir hul natuur en sewe vir mense se kultuur. Een is 'n gemengde terrein
items.bron: Category per site: iSimangaliso, Vredefort Dome, Cape Floral Region and Barberton Makhonjwa are natural (UNESCO/IUCN listings via SAnews, Mail & Guardian, BusinessLive, IUCN World Heritage Outlook); Robben Island, Mapungubwe, Fossil Hominid Sites, Richtersveld, ǂKhomani, Pleistocene Occupation Sites and the Mandela Legacy Sites are cultural; Maloti-Drakensberg Park is mixed (UNESCO decision 5133). 4 + 7 + 1 = 12.

items.bewering: Een is 'n gemengde terrein, want dit is op die lys vir sy natuur en ook vir die San se rotskuns.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Committee decision (whc.unesco.org/en/decisions/5133) and UNESCO document 217873: inscribed under cultural criteria (i)(iii) for its rock art and natural criteria (vii)(x); the rock art is San rock art.

items.bewering: Barberton Makhonjwa-berge: Mpumalanga
items.bron: BusinessLive 2 July 2018 and Vuk'uzenzele (vukuzenzele.gov.za, 'Mpumalanga boasts its first World Heritage Site'): inscribed 2018 for its geology, in Mpumalanga. Part of the wider greenstone belt runs into Eswatini, but the listed site is presented as Mpumalanga's.

items.bewering: Kaapse blommeryk: Wes-Kaap en Oos-Kaap
items.bron: IUCN World Heritage Outlook, Cape Floral Region Protected Areas (worldheritageoutlook.iucn.org/node/1130): a serial property spanning the Western and Eastern Cape; Baviaanskloof is one component.

items.bewering: iSimangaliso-vleilandpark: die Suid-Afrikaanse deel in KwaZulu-Natal
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 14 July 2025, and UNESCO documents: in July 2025 the Committee approved Mozambique's Maputo National Park as an extension of iSimangaliso, making it a transboundary property. So 'die Suid-Afrikaanse deel' is correct and up to date, and that part lies in KwaZulu-Natal (iSimangaliso inscribed 1999).

items.bewering: Vredefortkoepel: Vrystaat en Noordwes
items.bron: UNESCO nomination file 1162 (webarchive.unesco.org) and Government Gazette proclamation (gov.za): the site straddles the Vaal River, which forms the boundary between North West and the Free State.

items.bewering: Robbeneiland: Wes-Kaap
items.bron: southafrica.info 'World heritage in South Africa' and DIRCO's UNESCO page: cultural site, inscribed 1999, about 11 km off Cape Town.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe: Limpopo
items.bron: southafrica.info and DIRCO's UNESCO page: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape, inscribed 2003 as cultural, in Limpopo where the Limpopo and Shashe rivers meet.

items.bewering: Wieg van die Mensdom: Gauteng (grotte soos Sterkfontein), Noordwes (Taung) en Limpopo (Makapan-vallei)
items.bron: UNESCO data (whc.unesco.org/document/154587) and southafrica.info 'New sites for humankind's cradle': Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa - the Sterkfontein/Swartkrans/Kromdraai area in Gauteng (1999), extended in 2005 with Taung (North West) and the Makapan Valley (Limpopo). Sterkfontein is a cave site.

items.bewering: Richtersveld: Noord-Kaap
items.bron: DIRCO UNESCO page and South African reporting: Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape, inscribed 2007 as a cultural landscape (Nama pastoralism), in the Northern Cape. Despite 'Botanical' in the name it is listed as cultural, so placing it under cultural is right.

items.bewering: ǂKhomani-kulturele landskap: Noord-Kaap
items.bron: SA History Online, 'Khomani Cultural Landscape' (sahistory.org.za): inscribed 2017 as cultural, in the southern Kalahari in the Northern Cape, bordering Botswana and Namibia. One DIRCO page puts it in the 'Free State', which is plainly an error; every other source says Northern Cape.

items.bewering: Pleistoseen-bewoningsterreine (Pleistoseenbewoningsplekke): Wes-Kaap en KwaZulu-Natal
items.bron: The Presidency (gov.za) and Heritage Portal, July 2024: 'The Emergence of Modern Human Behaviour: The Pleistocene Occupation Sites of South Africa' - Diepkloof Rock Shelter and Pinnacle Point (Western Cape) and Sibhudu Cave (KwaZulu-Natal).

items.bewering: Nelson Mandela-erfenisterreine: 14 plekke in verskeie provinsies
items.bron: The Presidency media statement (gov.za, July 2024): 'Human Rights, Liberation and Reconciliation: Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites', a serial property of fourteen components in four provinces (Gauteng, Free State, Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal) and seven municipalities.

items.bewering: Maloti-Drakensbergpark: die Suid-Afrikaanse deel in KwaZulu-Natal
items.bron: UNESCO decision 5133 (2013 extension with Lesotho's Sehlabathebe National Park, making it transboundary) and Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife (kznparks.com, 'Maloti-Drakensberg Park World Heritage Site'): the South African part, the uKhahlamba-Drakensberg Park, is in KwaZulu-Natal.

items.bewering: Die Wieg van die Mensdom staan in Gauteng, Noordwes (Taung) en Limpopo (Makapan-vallei). Die Kaapse blommeryk staan in die Wes-Kaap en die Oos-Kaap. Die Vredefortkoepel staan in die Vrystaat en Noordwes. Die Pleistoseen-bewoningsterreine staan in die Wes-Kaap en KwaZulu-Natal. Die iSimangaliso-vleilandpark en die Maloti-Drakensbergpark staan met hul Suid-Afrikaanse deel in KwaZulu-Natal. Die Nelson Mandela-erfenisterreine staan as een aantekening, '14 plekke in verskeie provinsies'
items.bron: Same sources as the matching list items above. The map brief agrees with the lists in every province, and says each capital goes with its province, matching the gov.za list.

items.bewering: provinsie: Een van Suid-Afrika se nege dele, elk met sy eie regering.
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces': nine provinces, each with its own legislature, premier and executive council.

items.bewering: hoofstad: Die stad waar die regering van 'n provinsie of land sit.
items.bron: gov.za, 'South Africa's provinces' for the provincial capitals. The definition is right as a general one. South Africa itself splits its national capital three ways (Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein, per gov.za), but the lesson applies the word only to provinces, so a learner is not misled.

items.bewering: wêrelderfenisterrein: 'n Plek wat UNESCO erken omdat dit vir die hele mensdom waardevol is.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: properties are inscribed by the World Heritage Committee (under UNESCO's 1972 Convention) for 'outstanding universal value' to humanity. 'UNESCO erken' is an acceptable simplification for Grade 5.

items.bewering: natuurlike terrein: 'n Wêrelderfenisterrein wat op die lys is vir sy natuur, soos rotse of plante.
items.bron: UNESCO natural criteria (vii)-(x) cover geology, ecosystems and biodiversity. The examples fit this lesson's own sites: rocks (Vredefort, Barberton, natural criterion viii) and plants (Cape Floral Region, criteria ix and x), per the IUCN listings cited above.

items.bewering: kulturele terrein: 'n Wêrelderfenisterrein wat op die lys is vir sy kultuur, soos mense se verlede of hoe hulle leef.
items.bron: UNESCO cultural criteria (i)-(vi). Both examples fit sites in the lesson: the past (Mapungubwe, the fossil and Pleistocene sites) and a living way of life (Richtersveld's Nama pastoralism, the ǂKhomani San), per the sources above.

items.bewering: gemengde terrein: 'n Wêrelderfenisterrein wat vir sy natuur en ook vir sy kultuur erken is.
items.bron: UNESCO: mixed properties meet at least one natural and one cultural criterion. Maloti-Drakensberg is an example (decision 5133).

opsomming: Every checkable claim holds: the nine capitals match gov.za, and the count of twelve World Heritage sites (four natural, seven cultural, one mixed) and each site's province are confirmed against government, UNESCO and IUCN sources. 'The South African part' of iSimangaliso is correct, because Mozambique's Maputo National Park joined it in July 2025. Nothing new was added for South Africa in 2026. The lesson has no superlatives or comparisons. The count of twelve will go stale whenever UNESCO lists a new South African site, so check it again at each reprint.
